skill.name: hugging-face-cli
skill.description: Execute Hugging Face Hub workflows with the hf CLI, including authentication, downloads, uploads, repository management, cache maintenance, endpoints, and jobs.
skill.summary: Use the hf CLI to manage Hugging Face Hub models, datasets, spaces, cache, endpoints, and jobs.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The static analyzer mostly flagged Markdown backticks and Bash examples as executable code; these are false positives because SKILL.md is documentation. No prompt injection or hidden malware was found, but the skill documents destructive Hub operations, token handling, and remote compute workflows that need explicit safeguards.

remediation.issue: Destructive Hub commands are presented without mandatory confirmation guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Add instructions to request explicit user confirmation before repository deletion, file deletion, endpoint deletion, moves, or sync operations that use delete flags.

remediation.issue: Token and secret handling examples need stronger safety guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Recommend scoped tokens, avoid logging secrets, avoid pasting long-lived tokens, and verify trusted job images before passing HF_TOKEN to remote jobs.

remediation.issue: Remote job and endpoint examples can incur cost or run untrusted commands.
remediation.suggestion: Add preflight checks for account permissions, expected cost, resource flavor, trusted image source, and cancellation steps before running compute jobs.

remediation.issue: The package references additional command and workflow files that are not included.
remediation.suggestion: Include the referenced files or remove the links so users do not expect missing guidance.

semantic_findings.title: Destructive Hugging Face Operations Need Confirmation
semantic_findings.description: The skill documents commands that delete repositories, branches, tags, files, endpoints, and synced remote contents. Without explicit confirmation guidance, an agent could remove user assets during routine Hub management.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Multiple documented commands directly delete or replace Hub resources. The risk is operational misuse rather than hidden malicious code.

semantic_findings.title: Token and Remote Compute Handling Need Guardrails
semantic_findings.description: The skill documents token-based login, passing HF_TOKEN into remote jobs, and running user commands on Hugging Face infrastructure. Users need guidance for scoped tokens, trusted images, and cost controls.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited examples explicitly involve HF_TOKEN and remote job execution. These are legitimate features but can expose credentials or incur costs if used without controls.

content.user_title: Manage Hugging Face Hub from the CLI
content.value_statement: Hugging Face Hub work often requires many precise CLI commands. This skill helps users choose hf commands for downloads, uploads, repositories, cache, endpoints, and jobs.
actual_capabilities: Explains hf CLI authentication commands, including login, token use, account checks, and logout.
Provides commands for downloading models, datasets, spaces, revisions, and filtered file sets.
Shows upload workflows for files, folders, datasets, spaces, pull requests, and commit messages.
Lists repository operations for creation, privacy settings, branches, tags, moves, and deletion.
Covers cache inspection, cache removal, cache pruning, and checksum verification.
Documents endpoint management and Hugging Face Jobs commands for CPU or GPU workloads.
limitations: It depends on the hf CLI being installed and available in the user environment.
It does not verify Hugging Face account permissions before suggesting commands.
It does not execute safety checks before destructive or cost-incurring operations.
It references additional command and example files that are not included in this package.

use_cases.title: Download a model for local testing
use_cases.description: Select commands to download a full model, one file, or a pinned revision into a local directory.

use_cases.title: Publish training outputs to the Hub
use_cases.description: Create a private repository, upload artifacts, add tags, and use commit messages for release tracking.

use_cases.title: Operate Hub infrastructure
use_cases.description: List jobs, inspect logs, manage endpoints, and scale hosted inference resources during deployment work.

prompt_templates.title: Find the right download command
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner user needs a local copy of a Hub model.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me download a Hugging Face model with the hf CLI. Ask for the repo id, target folder, and revision if needed.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a safe upload workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: User wants to publish local files to a Hub repository.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan an hf CLI upload workflow for my folder. Include repository creation, privacy choice, commit message, and files to exclude.

prompt_templates.title: Audit cache and repository commands
prompt_templates.scenario: User wants to clean local cache and inspect Hub repositories.
prompt_templates.prompt: Show the hf CLI commands to review my cache, remove unused revisions, and list my model repositories without deleting anything.

prompt_templates.title: Design a controlled compute run
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced user needs remote Hugging Face Jobs or endpoint operations.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a guarded hf CLI plan for a remote GPU job or endpoint update. Include confirmation points, cost checks, and secret handling.

output_examples.input: I need to download one model file into a project folder.
output_examples.output: The response identifies the repo id, target file, local folder, and optional revision. It then gives a concise hf download command plan.

output_examples.input: I want to publish a private model release.
output_examples.output: The response outlines repository creation, private visibility, upload scope, commit message, and tag creation with a confirmation before upload.

output_examples.input: I need to run a GPU job using my Hugging Face token.
output_examples.output: The response asks for image, command, flavor, expected cost, and secret scope before suggesting a controlled remote job workflow.

best_practices: Confirm repository id, repo type, branch, and target path before upload, move, or delete operations.
Use private repositories for sensitive models or datasets until release permissions are reviewed.
Prefer scoped tokens and trusted container images for jobs, endpoints, and automated workflows.
anti_patterns: Do not run delete, move, sync, or endpoint deletion commands without explicit user confirmation.
Do not paste long-lived tokens into shared prompts, logs, shell history, or untrusted job images.
Do not upload the current directory before checking for secrets, generated logs, or private data.

faq.question: Does this skill install the Hugging Face CLI?
faq.answer: No. It documents hf CLI usage and assumes the CLI is already installed and authenticated when required.

faq.question: Can it download private models or datasets?
faq.answer: Yes, if the local hf CLI is authenticated with a token that has permission for the target repository.

faq.question: Can it upload files to the Hub?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers uploads for files, folders, datasets, spaces, pull requests, and custom commit messages.

faq.question: Does it include destructive commands?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents delete, move, and sync options, so users should require confirmation before running them.

faq.question: Can it manage Hugging Face cache?
faq.answer: Yes. It lists commands for viewing cache contents, removing revisions, pruning detached data, and verifying checksums.

faq.question: Can it help with Hugging Face Jobs and endpoints?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents job execution, logs, cancellation, endpoint deployment, pause, resume, scaling, and deletion.
